---
title: Spectral Methods
---

This page describes the spectral approximation tools implemented by the
[[numcosmo-math|NcmSpectral]] class: representing a function by its Chebyshev series,
computing the series adaptively, integrating and evaluating it, and building the banded
ultraspherical operators used to discretize linear differential operators following the
well-conditioned spectral method of @Olver2013.

## Chebyshev Representation

A function $f$ on an interval $[a,b]$ is approximated by a truncated Chebyshev series
in the Chebyshev variable
$$
s \equiv \frac{2x - (a+b)}{b-a} \in [-1,1],
\qquad
x = \frac{a+b}{2} + \frac{b-a}{2}\,s,
$$
so that
$$
f(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{N-1} c^k\,T_k(s),
\tag{1}
$$
where $T_k$ is the Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind and $c^k$ are the Chebyshev
coefficients. The forward and inverse maps
are [[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_x_to_s]] and [[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_s_to_x]].

## Computing the Coefficients

The coefficients in Eq. (1) are obtained by sampling $f$ at the Chebyshev--Lobatto
nodes
$$
s_j = \cos\!\left(\frac{j\pi}{N-1}\right),
\qquad
x_j = \frac{a+b}{2} + \frac{b-a}{2}\,s_j,
\qquad j = 0,\dots,N-1,
$$
and applying a type-I discrete cosine transform (FFTW `REDFT00`). The transform output
$\tilde c^k$ is normalized to the coefficients of Eq. (1) by
$$
c^0 = \frac{\tilde c^0}{2(N-1)},
\qquad
c^{N-1} = \frac{\tilde c^{N-1}}{2(N-1)},
\qquad
c^k = \frac{\tilde c^k}{N-1}\;\;(0 < k < N-1),
$$
the endpoint terms of the DCT-I on the Lobatto grid being halved. This fixed-order transform is
[[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_compute_chebyshev_coeffs]].

## Adaptive Refinement

The adaptive routines do not choose $N$ directly. They choose a refinement level $r$, a
non-negative integer, and use
$$
N = 2^r + 1
$$
nodes. The level is an exponent: raising $r$ by one doubles the number of intervals between
nodes, so the level arguments of the adaptive functions (`level_min`, `level_cap`) and the
`max-level` property count doublings of the grid, not coefficients. With this choice the
Lobatto grids are *nested*: the nodes at level $r$,
$$
s_j = \cos\!\left(\frac{j\pi}{2^r}\right),
\qquad j = 0,\dots,2^r,
$$
are a subset of those at level $r+1$. Refining therefore reuses every existing sample: the
previous values move to the even-indexed positions and only the new odd-indexed nodes are
evaluated, halving the number of function calls per level.

Starting from a minimum level $r_\mathrm{min}$ (`level_min`), the level is raised one step
at a time until the coefficients $c^k_{(r)}$ at level $r$ agree with the coefficients
$c^k_{(r-1)}$ at level $r-1$,
$$
\sum_{k \le 2^{r-1}} \left(c^k_{(r)} - c^k_{(r-1)}\right)^2
\;<\;
\max\!\left(
\varepsilon_\mathrm{rel}^2 \sum_{k \le 2^{r-1}} \left(c^k_{(r)}\right)^2,\;\;
\varepsilon_\mathrm{abs}^2
\right).
\tag{2}
$$
The sums run over the coarser level's $2^{r-1} + 1$ coefficients, the ones both expansions
carry. The entry point is [[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_compute_chebyshev_coeffs_adaptive]],
which returns the final level $r$.

$\varepsilon_\mathrm{abs}$ is measured in the units of the coefficients themselves and
is zero unless asked for, which leaves the relative test alone. It is for a caller that
knows $f$ to be negligible on $[a,b]$ against some larger quantity $f$ contributes to:
refining a term that cannot affect the result to full relative accuracy is pure cost,
and for a sharply varying $f$ it can exhaust `max-level`.

### When the tolerance is not met

The maximum level (`max-level`) is not a second stopping condition. It bounds the size
of the sample and transform buffers; Eq. (2) is what must end the refinement. Falling
out of the loop at `max-level` therefore means the coefficients on hand are
unconverged, and the three entry points differ only in what they do about that.

- [[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_compute_chebyshev_coeffs_adaptive]] takes
  $\varepsilon_\mathrm{rel}$ alone and treats reaching `max-level` as fatal. That is
  the right default for a caller expanding on one interval it cannot change: it has no
  recourse, so returning an unconverged series would only move the failure downstream,
  where its origin is no longer visible.
- [[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_compute_chebyshev_coeffs_adaptive_full]] adds
  $\varepsilon_\mathrm{abs}$ and is otherwise identical, fatal included. Passing zero
  reproduces the previous entry point exactly.
- [[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_compute_chebyshev_coeffs_adaptive_try]] accepts a cap
  $r_\mathrm{cap}$ (`level_cap`) of its own, at or below `max-level`, and reports through an output
  flag whether the tolerance was met rather than failing. It is for a caller that has a
  fallback, and for which not converging is information: not converging on a panel is
  how such a caller learns to subdivide, or to take a different route entirely. Its use
  in [UltraLevin](../specfunc/sbessel_projection.qmd) is to decide whether a fixed cell can be
  fitted directly, the alternative being to refit on a moving interval.

### Batch Expansions

When one evaluation yields several functions at once, expanding them separately repeats
that evaluation once per component, which is the whole cost whenever the evaluation is
what costs. [[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_compute_chebyshev_coeffs_batch_adaptive]]
takes an [[numcosmo-math|NcmSpectralFBatch]] instead, visits every node once, and
performs a single batched DCT-I over the interleaved components.

Convergence is judged per component and the component needing the highest level sets
it for all of them: the level is shared because the grid is. Sharing the grid
is also what leaves the resulting coefficients directly combinable, which is the point
when the components are to be summed or multiplied afterwards.
[[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_compute_chebyshev_coeffs_batch_adaptive_cap]] exposes a
cap and a fatal flag, for the same reasons as the scalar variants above.

The batch path keeps its own node and transform buffers on the
[[numcosmo-math|NcmSpectral]] instance and is therefore not reentrant: a fit performed
from inside the callback of a batch fit would overwrite the buffers of the fit that
called it, and must go through the single-function entry points. That is the second
reason [[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_compute_chebyshev_coeffs_adaptive_try]] is a
function of its own rather than a flag on the batch one.

## Spectral Integration

Integrating Eq. (1) term by term with
$$
\int_{-1}^{1} T_k(s)\,\mathrm{d}s =
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{2}{1-k^2}, & k \text{ even},\\[4pt]
0, & k \text{ odd},
\end{cases}
$$
gives
$$
\int_a^b f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x = \frac{b-a}{2}\sum_{k\ \mathrm{even}} \frac{2\,c^k}{1-k^2}.
$$
With the coefficients of the Lobatto transform this is Clenshaw--Curtis quadrature
[@Trefethen2008], which converges as fast as the coefficients decay. It is
[[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_chebyshev_integrate]]. The integral of a product $f g$ is
that of the expansion of $f g$ itself; when one evaluation gives both factors, the
batch expansion fits them together.

## Evaluation

A Chebyshev series is evaluated with the Clenshaw recurrence. For interior points $|s|
< 0.9$,
$$
b_k = 2s\,b_{k+1} - b_{k+2} + c^k,
\qquad
f = s\,b_1 - b_2 + c^0,
$$
run downward from $k = N-1$ with $b_N = b_{N+1} = 0$. Near the endpoints the plain
recurrence loses accuracy through cancellation, so the Reinsch modification is used
instead, propagating the differenced quantities $d_k$ and $e_k = d_k \pm e_{k+1}$ with
the shifted argument $s \mp 1$. Exactly at $s = \pm 1$ the closed forms $T_k(1) = 1$
and $T_k(-1) = (-1)^k$ are summed directly. Evaluation is
[[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_chebyshev_eval]] (and
[[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_chebyshev_eval_x]] for an argument in $[a,b]$).

The derivative is obtained without explicitly forming the derivative series. The
coefficients $c'^k$ of $f'(s) = \sum_k c'^k T_k(s)$ satisfy
$$
c'^k = \sum_{\substack{j > k \\ j-k\ \mathrm{odd}}} 2j\,c^j\;\;(k\ge 1),
\qquad
c'^0 = \sum_{\substack{j\ \mathrm{odd}}} j\,c^j,
$$
and are folded into a single fused backward Clenshaw pass in
[[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_chebyshev_deriv]]. The chain rule supplies the derivative
with respect to the physical variable, $\mathrm{d}f/\mathrm{d}x =
(2/(b-a))\,\mathrm{d}f/\mathrm{d}s$, in
[[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_chebyshev_deriv_x]].

## Rebasing to Another Interval

A series computed on $[a_\mathrm{in}, b_\mathrm{in}]$ can be re-expressed on a
different interval without evaluating $f$ again. Writing $s_\mathrm{in}$ for the
Chebyshev variable of the source interval and $s_\mathrm{out}$ for that of the target,
$s_\mathrm{in} = \alpha s_\mathrm{out} + \beta$ is affine, so each $T_k(s_\mathrm{in})$
expands in the $T_j(s_\mathrm{out})$ through the Chebyshev recurrence applied to that
affine argument. [[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_chebyshev_rebase]] runs the recurrence and
costs $O(n^2)$ in the number of coefficients kept.

The target interval need not lie inside the source one. Outside it the result is the
polynomial's own continuation, which is what makes a rebase usable as a smooth
extension of a fit, but only for a short series. Once $|s_\mathrm{in}| > 1$ the Chebyshev
polynomials grow like $\left(|s_\mathrm{in}| + \sqrt{s_\mathrm{in}^2-1}\right)^k$, so widening the interval by a
factor $\alpha$ amplifies the coefficient of $T_k$ by about $\left(\alpha +
\sqrt{\alpha^2-1}\right)^k$: at $\alpha = 2$ that is $3.7^k$, and a coefficient sitting
at roundoff level in a degree-65 fit returns larger than the function it belongs to.
The function returns $\sum_j |c_\mathrm{out}^j|$, the sum over the rebased coefficients,
which bounds $|f|$ over the whole target interval
and is the cheapest way to tell a continuation apart from amplified roundoff.

## Ultraspherical Bases

The differential operators below produce their output in an *ultraspherical*
(Gegenbauer) basis $C^{(\lambda)}_n$ rather than in the Chebyshev basis. Two cases are
used:

- $\lambda = 1$: $C^{(1)}_n = U_n$, the Chebyshev polynomials of the second
  kind, with $U_n(\pm 1) = (n+1)(\pm 1)^n$ and the recurrence
  $U_{n+1} = 2s\,U_n - U_{n-1}$.
- $\lambda = 2$: $C^{(2)}_n$, with $C^{(2)}_0 = 1$, $C^{(2)}_1 = 4s$,
  endpoint values $C^{(2)}_n(\pm 1) = \binom{n+3}{3}(\pm 1)^n$, and the
  recurrence
  $(n+1)\,C^{(2)}_{n+1} = 2(n+2)\,s\,C^{(2)}_n - (n+3)\,C^{(2)}_{n-1}$.

Conversion from the Chebyshev to the $\lambda=1$ basis uses the identity $U_n - U_{n-2}
= 2T_n$, i.e. $T_n = \tfrac12\!\left(C^{(1)}_n - C^{(1)}_{n-2}\right)$ for $n \ge 2$
(with $T_0 = C^{(1)}_0$ and $T_1 = \tfrac12 C^{(1)}_1$), giving the map
$g^k = \tfrac12(c^k - c^{k+2})$ from the Chebyshev coefficients $c^k$ to the
$C^{(1)}$ coefficients $g^k$. Conversion to the $\lambda=2$ basis, whose coefficients are
also written $g^k$,
$$
g^k = \tfrac12 c^0\,\delta_{k,0}
    + \frac{c^k}{2(k+1)}
    - \frac{(k+2)\,c^{k+2}}{(k+1)(k+3)}
    + \frac{c^{k+4}}{2(k+3)},
$$
is the projection (identity) operator written between bases. These are
[[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_chebT_to_gegenbauer_alpha1]] and
[[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_chebT_to_gegenbauer_alpha2]]; the corresponding series are
evaluated by [[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_gegenbauer_alpha1_eval]] and
[[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_gegenbauer_alpha2_eval]] with the same Clenshaw strategy
as above.

Two derivative maps are tabulated on their own because they reduce to something
shorter than a general composition. Combining $T_n' = n\,C^{(1)}_{n-1}$ with the ladder
$C^{(1)}_m = \left(C^{(2)}_m - C^{(2)}_{m-2}\right)/(m+1)$ leaves the two-term rule
$g^k = c^{k+1} - c^{k+3}$ for the $C^{(2)}$ coefficients of $f'$, and $T_n'' =
2n\,C^{(2)}_{n-2}$ makes the second derivative diagonal, $g^k = 2(k+2)\,c^{k+2}$. These
are [[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_chebT_deriv_to_gegenbauer_alpha2]] and
[[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_chebT_deriv2_to_gegenbauer_alpha2]]; both differentiate
with respect to $s$, leaving the chain-rule factor $2/(b-a)$ per derivative to the
caller. Multiplication by an affine factor without leaving the $C^{(2)}$ basis, from
the recurrence
$$
s\,C^{(2)}_n = \frac{(n+1)\,C^{(2)}_{n+1} + (n+3)\,C^{(2)}_{n-1}}{2(n+2)},
$$
is [[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_gegenbauer_alpha2_mul_affine]].

## Ultraspherical Operators

The well-conditioned spectral method of @Olver2013 represents a linear differential
operator as a *banded* matrix by mapping the Chebyshev coefficients $c^k$ of $f$ to the
$C^{(2)}$ coefficients $g^k$ of the transformed function. Written as a matrix,
$$
g^k = \sum_i M^k{}_i\,c^i,
$$
and each row of the table below is row $k$ of $M$; the matrix functions return $M$
truncated to $N \times N$. Each operator below is banded
(bandwidth $\le 9$) and adds into a shared row buffer, so that a full operator such as
$p_2(s)\,f'' + p_1(s)\,f' + p_0(s)\,f$ with polynomial coefficients up to degree two is
assembled as a banded linear combination of these primitives. Throughout the table
$c^k \equiv 0$ for $k < 0$, so a term whose index runs off the start vanishes.

| Operator | $C^{(2)}$ coefficient of the output | Method |
|---|---|---|
| identity | $\dfrac{c^k}{2(k+1)} - \dfrac{(k+2)c^{k+2}}{(k+1)(k+3)} + \dfrac{c^{k+4}}{2(k+3)} + \tfrac12 c^0\,\delta_{k,0}$ | [[numcosmo-math\|ncm_spectral_get_proj_matrix]] |
| $s$ | $\dfrac{c^{k-1}}{4(k+1)} - \dfrac{c^{k+1}}{4(k+3)} - \dfrac{c^{k+3}}{4(k+1)} + \dfrac{c^{k+5}}{4(k+3)} + \tfrac14 c^1\,\delta_{k,0} + \tfrac18 c^0\,\delta_{k,1}$ | [[numcosmo-math\|ncm_spectral_get_s_matrix]] |
| $s^2$ | $\dfrac{c^{k-2}}{8(k+1)} + \dfrac{c^k}{4(k+1)(k+3)} - \dfrac{(k+2)c^{k+2}}{4(k+1)(k+3)} - \dfrac{c^{k+4}}{4(k+1)(k+3)} + \dfrac{c^{k+6}}{8(k+3)} + \big(\tfrac1{12}c^0 + \tfrac18 c^2\big)\delta_{k,0} + \tfrac1{16}c^1\,\delta_{k,1} + \tfrac1{24}c^0\,\delta_{k,2}$ | [[numcosmo-math\|ncm_spectral_get_s2_matrix]] |
| $\mathrm{d}/\mathrm{d}s$ | $c^{k+1} - c^{k+3}$ | [[numcosmo-math\|ncm_spectral_get_d_matrix]] |
| $s\,\mathrm{d}/\mathrm{d}s$ | $\dfrac{k\,c^k}{2(k+1)} + \dfrac{(k+2)c^{k+2}}{(k+1)(k+3)} - \dfrac{(k+4)c^{k+4}}{2(k+3)}$ | [[numcosmo-math\|ncm_spectral_get_s_d_matrix]] |
| $\mathrm{d}^2/\mathrm{d}s^2$ | $2(k+2)\,c^{k+2}$ | [[numcosmo-math\|ncm_spectral_get_d2_matrix]] |
| $s\,\mathrm{d}^2/\mathrm{d}s^2$ | $k\,c^{k+1} + (k+4)\,c^{k+3}$ | [[numcosmo-math\|ncm_spectral_get_s_d2_matrix]] |
| $s^2\,\mathrm{d}^2/\mathrm{d}s^2$ | $\dfrac{k(k-1)c^k}{2(k+1)} + \dfrac{(k+2)\big((k+2)^2-3\big)c^{k+2}}{(k+1)(k+3)} + \dfrac{(k+4)(k+5)c^{k+4}}{2(k+3)}$ | [[numcosmo-math\|ncm_spectral_get_s2_d2_matrix]] |

Every row holds for all $k$ as written. The Kronecker-delta terms are the $T_0$ and
$T_1$ special cases of Chebyshev multiplication, which contribute only to the first one
to three rows of an operator.

The single-row builders ([[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_compute_proj_row]] and the
companions) expose the same coefficients for assembling custom combinations.
